Credentials Report or Access Advisor: which one to use for what?

The Credentials Report is account-level: it lists all IAM users and the status of their passwords, access keys and MFA, for audit and compliance; it can be downloaded via the console, API, CLI or SDK and is regenerated at most every 4 hours. Access Advisor is user-level: it shows the services granted and the date of last access, which lets you trim policies down to least privilege.
4 hours
What is iam:PassRole for?

When a user configures a service with a role (EC2 instance, Lambda...), you need to control which roles they can pass, otherwise they can escalate by attaching a more powerful role. So you grant iam:PassRole on a list of approved roles, for example role/EC2-roles-for-*. PassRole is not an API call and leaves no CloudTrail trace of its own: you look at the log of the call that created or modified the resource.

Why IAM Roles Anywhere rather than IAM users for an on-premises server?

The access keys of an IAM user never expire, leak easily and are hard to rotate. With Roles Anywhere, the server presents an X.509 certificate validated by a trust anchor (for example AWS Private CA) and receives temporary credentials through a profile and a role. They expire on their own and you reuse the same roles and policies as in AWS.

What does IAM Access Analyzer do?

It defines a zone of trust (account or Organization) and creates findings when a resource is accessible from outside: S3 buckets, IAM roles, KMS keys, Lambda functions and layers, SQS queues, secrets. It also validates policies (warnings, errors, suggestions) and can generate a policy from 90 days of CloudTrail activity.
